questions.question: How many bits are in a nibble and a byte?
questions.answer: A nibble has 4 bits and a byte has 8 bits.
questions.explanation: A nibble has 4 bits and a byte has 8 bits.

questions.question: What does an IDE's run-time environment let you do?
questions.answer: D — Run and test code
questions.explanation: It lets you run the program and inspect its behaviour or output.

questions.question: How do IDE error diagnostics help?
questions.answer: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.
questions.explanation: They show errors and often their location, helping the programmer find the cause.

questions.question: Two computers receive the same byte but show different characters. Why? What must match?
questions.answer: The computers use different character sets or encodings. To show the same letter, both need a matching encoding.
questions.explanation: The computers use different character sets or encodings. To show the same letter, both need a matching encoding.

questions.question: Convert 00101101 binary to denary.
What is a character set?
questions.answer: A — Characters linked to codes
questions.explanation: A character set defines characters and the codes used to represent them.

questions.question: “A record must contain only one unnamed value.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.
questions.explanation: Named fields about one item or person. Fields may have different data types.

questions.question: Valid ages are 13–18. Changing <18 to <=18 fixes a bug. Give three tests near 18 and their expected results. Why retest a value that worked before?
questions.answer: 17 accepted; 18 accepted; 19 rejected. Retest a value that worked before to check for regression: a new fault caused by the fix.
questions.explanation: 17 accepted; 18 accepted; 19 rejected. Retest a value that worked before to check for regression: a new fault caused by the fix.

questions.question: Why does 11111111 plus 00000001 overflow eight bits?
questions.answer: The true sum is 256, requiring nine bits; only eight stored bits would contain 00000000.
questions.explanation: The true sum is 256, requiring nine bits; only eight stored bits would contain 00000000.

questions.question: A has code 65. Capital-letter codes go in order. What is D's code?
questions.explanation: D is three places after A, so 65 + 3 = 68.

questions.question: “Unicode supports fewer characters than standard ASCII.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Unicode supports far more characters than standard ASCII.
questions.explanation: Unicode supports far more characters than standard ASCII.

questions.question: A program calculates an area and shows a menu in several places. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) A function cannot return a value. (b) A procedure must return a value.
questions.answer: (a) A function returns a value, such as an area. (b) A procedure performs a task, such as showing a menu, without returning a value. Use arguments and return values to avoid unwanted changes to global data.
questions.explanation: (a) A function returns a value, such as an area. (b) A procedure performs a task, such as showing a menu, without returning a value. Use arguments and return values to avoid unwanted changes to global data.

questions.question: Convert hexadecimal A3 to eight-bit binary.
How many different codes can 7 bits represent?
questions.explanation: There are 2^7 = 128 different patterns.

questions.question: “Metadata is another name for the colour of every pixel.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Extra image details, such as width, height or colour depth. These are separate from pixel data.
questions.explanation: Extra image details, such as width, height or colour depth. These are separate from pixel data.

questions.question: (a) A bitmap uses 5 bits per pixel. How many colours can it show? What if you add one bit? (b) A 50 × 20 pixel image doubles in width and height. Colour depth stays the same. How do pixel count and raw size change? Explain.
questions.answer: (a) 32 colours; one extra bit doubles this to 64. (b) 1,000 pixels become 4,000. Raw size is four times larger: both dimensions double.
questions.explanation: (a) 32 colours; one extra bit doubles this to 64. (b) 1,000 pixels become 4,000. Raw size is four times larger: both dimensions double.

questions.question: How does a bitmap represent pixel colours?
questions.answer: Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.
questions.explanation: Each pixel has a colour code stored in binary.

questions.question: Why can heavy virtual-memory use slow a program?
questions.answer: D — Secondary storage is slower
questions.explanation: Moving data between RAM and slower secondary storage adds delays.

questions.question: “A parameter is the final printed output of every program.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.explanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.question: A microphone records digital sound. “Sampling stores every instant of the sound wave.” Correct this. How does it affect recorded detail?
questions.answer: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.
questions.explanation: Measure amplitude at regular intervals. Store each rounded (quantised) value in binary. Sample rate and bit depth limit the detail captured.

questions.question: What does lossy compression do?
questions.answer: It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.
questions.explanation: It discards some information, so the exact original cannot necessarily be restored.

questions.question: What does RAM hold while a program runs?
questions.answer: A — Active instructions and data
questions.explanation: RAM holds the program's working data and instructions. It is volatile.

questions.question: “Sample rate is the number of bits used for each sample.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Sample rate is samples per second. At 8,000 Hz, 8,000 samples are taken each second. A higher rate can capture more detail but uses more space.
questions.explanation: Sample rate is samples per second. At 8,000 Hz, 8,000 samples are taken each second. A higher rate can capture more detail but uses more space.

questions.question: Two recordings have the same sample rate and length but different bit depths. “Bit depth is samples per second.” Correct this. How does bit depth affect detail and size?
questions.answer: Bit depth is bits per sample. More bits allow more amplitude levels but use more space. Longer duration adds samples; sample rate and bit depth control detail.
questions.explanation: Bit depth is bits per sample. More bits allow more amplitude levels but use more space. Longer duration adds samples; sample rate and bit depth control detail.

questions.question: What is abstraction?
questions.answer: Removing irrelevant detail while keeping what is needed to solve the problem.
questions.explanation: Removing irrelevant detail while keeping what is needed to solve the problem.

questions.question: What does WHERE do in SQL?
questions.answer: B — Filters rows
questions.explanation: WHERE keeps rows that meet the stated condition.

questions.question: A zero-indexed 2D array is [[11,12],[21,22]]. Give grid[1,0], then state the indexes needed to access 12.
questions.answer: grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].
questions.explanation: grid[1,0] is 21; 12 is at grid[0,1].

questions.question: Two mono recordings have the same sample rate and bit depth. One lasts twice as long. Does this double its quality? How does raw size change?
questions.answer: Raw size doubles: there are twice as many samples. Quality does not improve. Sample rate and bit depth stay the same.
questions.explanation: Raw size doubles: there are twice as many samples. Quality does not improve. Sample rate and bit depth stay the same.

questions.question: What does a diamond represent in a flowchart?
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: In OCR ERL, which value can random(1,6) return?
questions.explanation: It can return any integer from 1 to 6, including both endpoints.
topics: Generate and use bounded random integers

questions.question: “A USB flash drive stores data on a rotating magnetic platter.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.
questions.explanation: Solid-state storage with no moving read/write mechanism.

questions.question: A large file must cross a slow link. “Compression always makes files larger.” Correct this. How might compression affect transfer time?
questions.answer: A smaller file uses less storage and can be sent faster over the same link. Compression and decompression take processing time.
questions.explanation: A smaller file uses less storage and can be sent faster over the same link. Compression and decompression take processing time.

questions.question: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.answer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.explanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.question: What does lossy compression remove?
questions.answer: D — Some original information
questions.explanation: Lossy compression discards information, so the exact original may not be restored.

questions.question: “Changing a variable name automatically fixes every logic error.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.
questions.explanation: Clear names show what values mean and help people read and change code.

questions.question: A program is compressed before being sent. “Lossless compression removes source-code characters.” Correct this. Why does it matter here?
questions.answer: Lossless compression restores every character exactly. Losing characters could break the program. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code cannot.
questions.explanation: Lossless compression restores every character exactly. Losing characters could break the program. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code cannot.

questions.question: Does linear search require a sorted list?
questions.answer: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.
questions.explanation: No; it examines items in sequence until a match is found or the list ends.

questions.question: What is decomposition?
questions.answer: A — Splitting a problem into parts
questions.explanation: Break a large problem into smaller, manageable subproblems.

questions.question: “Every local variable can always be accessed directly from every other subprogram.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.
questions.explanation: A local variable can be used only within its own subprogram or local scope.

questions.question: Several procedures share a global score. “A global variable can be read only in one subprogram.” Correct this. What risk does sharing it create?
questions.answer: Global variables can be used across the program. This risks unwanted changes and makes faults harder to trace. Use arguments and return values to avoid hidden changes.
questions.explanation: Global variables can be used across the program. This risks unwanted changes and makes faults harder to trace. Use arguments and return values to avoid hidden changes.

questions.question: What must be true before binary search is used?
questions.answer: The list must be sorted. This lets the search safely rule out half the remaining items.

questions.question: What does the MAR hold?
questions.answer: B — The address being accessed
questions.explanation: The Memory Address Register holds the address of the memory location being accessed.

questions.question: “Functions can return only one digit and can never return an array.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.
questions.explanation: Yes. A subprogram can receive an array; a function can return an array.

questions.question: A café program finds the cost of identical drinks. “Inputs are the final results.” Correct this. Give the inputs, process and output.
questions.answer: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiply them. Output: total cost. Inputs come before the calculation; the output comes after it.
questions.explanation: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiply them. Output: total cost. Inputs come before the calculation; the output comes after it.

questions.question: When does ascending bubble sort swap two adjacent items?
questions.answer: When the left item is greater than the right item.
questions.explanation: When the left item is greater than the right item.

questions.question: What does readLine() do on an open text file?
questions.answer: C — Reads the next line
questions.explanation: It reads the next line and advances the current file position.

questions.question: “Primary storage exists only to keep long-term backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.
questions.explanation: It holds instructions and working data that the CPU needs while programs run.

questions.question: “My unsaved work will survive a power cut because this computer has ROM.” Explain the mistake. How could the work have been kept?
questions.answer: Unsaved work is in volatile RAM, so it is lost when power goes off. Save it to non-volatile secondary storage to keep it.
questions.explanation: Unsaved work is in volatile RAM, so it is lost when power goes off. Save it to non-volatile secondary storage to keep it.

questions.question: What does insertion sort do with the next unsorted item?
questions.answer: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.
questions.explanation: Place the next item in the correct position in the sorted part. Shift larger items right.

questions.question: What is ROM commonly used to store?
questions.answer: D — Startup instructions
questions.explanation: ROM keeps firmware or startup instructions when power is off.

questions.question: “Cache is a remote Internet server that replaces CPU registers.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.
questions.explanation: Cache is in or near the CPU. It gives faster access to often-used data and instructions than main memory.

questions.question: A pupil restarts a computer to open saved work. “RAM keeps every file forever.” Correct this. Why is secondary storage needed?
questions.answer: Secondary storage keeps files and programs without power. Save the work there before restarting.
questions.explanation: Secondary storage keeps files and programs without power. Save the work there before restarting.

questions.question: How does merge sort combine two sorted lists?
questions.answer: Compare the next item in each list. Take the smaller. Repeat, then add any items left over.
questions.explanation: Compare the next item in each list. Take the smaller. Repeat, then add any items left over.

questions.question: Code has a missing bracket. “A syntax error is a wrong result from code that follows the language's rules.” Correct this. What needs fixing?
questions.answer: A syntax error breaks the language's rules and stops the affected code being translated or run. Fix it, then trace and test the logic.
questions.explanation: A syntax error breaks the language's rules and stops the affected code being translated or run. Fix it, then trace and test the logic.

questions.question: Which CPU component performs arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.answer: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question: Why might an HDD suit a large archive?
questions.answer: B — Low cost per GB
questions.explanation: An HDD can provide lots of storage at a low cost per GB.

questions.question: “An SSD is faster because its magnetic read head rotates more quickly.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.
questions.explanation: It does not need a moving head to seek positions on spinning platters.

questions.question: A laptop is used on a bumpy bus. “Portability and durability mean the same thing.” Correct this. How should this affect the storage choice?
questions.answer: Durability means resisting damage; portability means being easy to carry. An SSD has no moving read/write parts, so it handles shocks better. Size and weight also matter.
questions.explanation: Durability means resisting damage; portability means being easy to carry. An SSD has no moving read/write parts, so it handles shocks better. Size and weight also matter.

questions.question: For s = 'COMPUTER', what is s.substring(1,3) in OCR ERL?
questions.answer: OMP; indexing starts at zero and the second argument gives length.
questions.explanation: OMP; indexing starts at zero and the second argument gives length.

questions.question: Which is an output from a greeting program?
questions.answer: C — A displayed greeting
questions.explanation: The displayed greeting is produced by the program. The other actions supply input.

questions.question: “Duplicating the same long code block everywhere always improves maintainability.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Related logic can be reused, understood, tested and changed in one place.
questions.explanation: Related logic can be reused, understood, tested and changed in one place.

questions.question: Nested IF statements are hard to read. “Indentation proves the logic is correct.” Correct this. How does indentation help?
questions.answer: Indentation shows blocks and nesting. Some languages require it. It helps people read and change code, but does not prove the logic is correct.
questions.explanation: Indentation shows blocks and nesting. Some languages require it. It helps people read and change code, but does not prove the logic is correct.

questions.question: How is a cell selected in a two-dimensional array?
questions.answer: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.
questions.explanation: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.

questions.question: What should a useful code comment explain?
questions.answer: D — Why the code is needed
questions.explanation: Useful comments explain intent or reasoning to help others understand the code.

questions.question: “The CPU's main purpose is permanent file storage.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It executes instructions to process data.

questions.question: What happens in the fetch stage?
questions.answer: A — Get the next instruction
questions.explanation: The CPU gets the next instruction from memory.

questions.question: “Execution only copies an instruction into memory without performing it.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.
questions.explanation: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.

questions.question: “The Control Unit stores your documents forever.” Correct this. Explain its role when the CPU runs an instruction.
questions.answer: The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. The ALU processes data; registers store it briefly.
questions.explanation: The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. The ALU processes data; registers store it briefly.

questions.question: Why open a file before reading it?
questions.answer: Opening establishes a handle or connection through which the program accesses the file.
questions.explanation: Opening establishes a handle or connection through which the program accesses the file.

questions.question: What does CPU cache hold?
questions.answer: B — Often-used data and instructions
questions.explanation: Cache holds frequently or recently used data and instructions for fast access.

questions.question: “A register is a large external drive used for backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
questions.explanation: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.

questions.question: The next instruction is at address 240. An addition gives 18. What do the accumulator and Program Counter hold? Explain the difference.
questions.answer: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.
questions.explanation: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.

questions.question: What does SELECT specify in an SQL query?
questions.answer: The fields (columns) to return.
questions.explanation: The fields (columns) to return.

questions.question: What does a higher CPU clock speed mean?
questions.answer: C — More cycles per second
questions.explanation: Clock speed measures CPU clock cycles per second.

questions.question: “Larger cache increases the number of installed CPU cores.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.
questions.explanation: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.

questions.question: CPU A: 4 GHz, two cores, 2 MB cache. CPU B: 3 GHz, eight cores, 8 MB cache. Why is neither fastest for every task?
questions.answer: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.

questions.question: Which integers can random(1,6) produce in OCR ERL?

questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: A program works out a bill, then applies a discount. “The order of steps never matters.” Correct this. What could go wrong?
questions.answer: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.
questions.explanation: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.

questions.question: In a trace table, should you record executed variable updates or only variable names?
questions.answer: Executed variable updates in their actual order.

questions.question: Which description matches a NOT gate symbol?

questions.answer: Q: 1, 0. Double NOT: 0, 1, restoring A.

questions.question: After one ascending bubble-sort pass on [7, 3, 6, 2], what is the list?

questions.question: “An IF statement must execute every possible branch regardless of its condition.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.

questions.question: What does authentication establish?
questions.answer: Whether a user has supplied suitable evidence of the claimed identity.

questions.question: Why translate high-level source code?

questions.answer: It is built into a larger device for a specific task, often with limited resources.

questions.explanation: Each input has two possible values, so 2^3 = 8 combinations.

questions.answer: 12 is an integer but outside the valid range, so it must be rejected.

questions.question: How can a loop total an array's values?
questions.answer: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.
questions.explanation: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.

questions.question: Why is a thermostat controller an embedded system?
questions.answer: A — It has a specific task
questions.explanation: It is part of a heating system and controls temperature.

questions.question: “DNS assigns the same MAC address to all computers visiting a website.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Distributed DNS servers help look up the IP address associated with a domain name.
questions.explanation: Distributed DNS servers help look up the IP address associated with a domain name.

questions.question: RAM is full. Apps keep moving data between RAM and an SSD. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Virtual memory needs no secondary storage. (b) Virtual memory is faster than RAM because SSDs hold more.
questions.answer: (a) Virtual memory uses secondary storage when RAM is too full. (b) Moving data between RAM and slower secondary storage takes time. More storage space does not mean faster access.

questions.question: What is a parameter?
questions.answer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.explanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.question: Which is a benefit of a high-level language?
questions.answer: B — Easier for humans to read
questions.explanation: High-level code is closer to human language and is usually easier to read and maintain.

questions.question: “Adding active users always increases the bandwidth available to each user.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.
questions.explanation: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.

questions.question: A school needs central accounts and shared files. Three club laptops share files directly. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Every client must be a dedicated server. (b) Peer-to-peer needs a central server.
questions.answer: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.

questions.question: What does WHERE do in an SQL query?
questions.answer: It selects rows that meet a condition.
questions.explanation: It selects rows that meet a condition.

questions.question: When does a compiler translate source code?
questions.answer: C — Before the program runs
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the program before execution, producing code that can run again.

questions.question: “A router's main job is executing spreadsheet formulas.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It forwards traffic between different networks using IP addressing.
questions.explanation: It forwards traffic between different networks using IP addressing.

questions.question: A computer sends data to a printer on its LAN. “A switch sends every unicast frame to every port.” Correct this. How should the data reach the printer?
questions.answer: A switch uses MAC addresses to send data to the right connected device. It does not normally send each known unicast frame to every port.
questions.explanation: A switch uses MAC addresses to send data to the right connected device. It does not normally send each known unicast frame to every port.

questions.question: A £5-per-ticket program uses total = tickets + 5. What is the correction?
questions.answer: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.
questions.explanation: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.

questions.question: What does an IDE's run-time environment let you do?
questions.answer: D — Run and test code
questions.explanation: It lets you run the program and inspect its behaviour or output.

questions.question: “An IPv4 address is always six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.
questions.explanation: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.

questions.question: An IDE finds a missing bracket. Once fixed, the program runs but gives the wrong total. Why did the IDE not prove the logic correct? What should you do next?
questions.answer: The IDE found a syntax error, not a logic error. Trace the calculation. Test inputs with known totals and compare results.
questions.explanation: The IDE found a syntax error, not a logic error. Trace the calculation. Test inputs with known totals and compare results.

What is the Internet?

questions.question: “A web client must host every website before it can request a page.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A server stores and makes website resources available for clients to request.
questions.explanation: A server stores and makes website resources available for clients to request.

questions.question: A pupil needs work on several devices. “Cloud files are always available when the Internet fails.” Correct this. What could happen?
questions.answer: Cloud resources are accessed over a network. Files may be unavailable if the connection or server fails.
questions.explanation: Cloud resources are accessed over a network. Files may be unavailable if the connection or server fails.

questions.question: What distinguishes a WAN?
questions.answer: A WAN links networks over a large area, often using links provided by other organisations.
questions.explanation: A WAN links networks over a large area, often using links provided by other organisations.

questions.question: Why use shared computing standards?
questions.answer: B — Different products work together
questions.explanation: Agreed rules and interfaces let products from different makers communicate.

questions.question: “SMTP's role is synchronising folders and read status across mail clients.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.
questions.explanation: Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.

questions.question: A star LAN has one central switch. “One broken workstation cable stops the whole network.” Correct this. Compare a broken cable with a failed switch.
questions.answer: A broken workstation cable usually affects just that device. If the central switch fails, devices using it lose contact. Available paths determine which connections still work.
questions.explanation: A broken workstation cable usually affects just that device. If the central switch fails, devices using it lose contact. Available paths determine which connections still work.

questions.question: What does a wireless access point do?
questions.answer: It enables wireless devices to connect to the network.
questions.explanation: It enables wireless devices to connect to the network.

questions.question: Why can a mesh survive some broken links?
questions.answer: C — It has other paths
questions.explanation: Alternative routes can keep communication working after some links fail.

questions.question: “Fibre carries electrical signals through copper wire.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Fibre uses light. It supports fast data transfer over long distances and resists electromagnetic interference. Installation can cost more.
questions.explanation: Fibre uses light. It supports fast data transfer over long distances and resists electromagnetic interference. Installation can cost more.

questions.question: Desktops and moving tablets need network links. “Wi-Fi needs a cable from each tablet to the switch.” Correct this. Which links suit these devices?
questions.answer: Ethernet uses cables. Wi-Fi uses radio, so tablets can move around, but interference can affect it. Choose links to suit the distance and data rate needed.

questions.question: What is FTP used for?
questions.answer: Transferring files between networked computers.
questions.explanation: Transferring files between networked computers.

questions.question: How does phishing trick people?
questions.answer: D — Pretends to be trusted
questions.explanation: A fake trusted message tricks someone into revealing data or taking an unsafe action.

questions.question: “Bluetooth is normally the best choice for a high-capacity link between distant school sites.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Bluetooth suits short-range links, such as keyboards or headphones. Check range, data rate and power needs.
questions.explanation: Bluetooth suits short-range links, such as keyboards or headphones. Check range, data rate and power needs.

questions.question: A network shows 2001:db8::7. “IPv6 uses four decimal numbers separated by dots.” Correct this. How is this address written?
questions.answer: IPv6 uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Groups of zeros can be shortened. Routers use IP addresses between networks; switches use MAC addresses within a LAN.
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Groups of zeros can be shortened. Routers use IP addresses between networks; switches use MAC addresses within a LAN.

questions.question: How can more active users affect network performance?
questions.answer: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.
questions.explanation: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.

questions.question: How does a brute-force attack work?
questions.answer: A — Tries many possible passwords
questions.explanation: It repeatedly tries possible passwords or keys until one succeeds.

questions.question: “A MAC address is the text domain name entered into a browser.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A MAC address identifies a network interface on a LAN. It is usually six pairs of hexadecimal digits.
questions.explanation: A MAC address identifies a network interface on a LAN. It is usually six pairs of hexadecimal digits.

questions.question: Data must reach another network in the right order. “TCP chooses fonts; IP draws images.” Correct this. Explain each protocol's job.
questions.answer: TCP supports reliable delivery in order. IP handles addressing and routing between networks. Each protocol has its own job; encryption does not prove a site is honest.
questions.explanation: TCP supports reliable delivery in order. IP handles addressing and routing between networks. Each protocol has its own job; encryption does not prove a site is honest.

questions.question: What is the concept of SQL injection?
questions.answer: Unsafe input changes an SQL query. An attacker may then view or change data.
questions.explanation: Unsafe input changes an SQL query. An attacker may then view or change data.

questions.question: What does a firewall control?
questions.answer: B — Allowed network traffic
questions.explanation: A firewall uses rules to allow or block network traffic.

questions.question: “HTTP is the protocol used only to send email to a mail server.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Transferring web resources between web clients and servers.
questions.explanation: Transferring web resources between web clients and servers.

questions.question: A pupil logs in to a website. “HTTPS proves every website is honest.” Correct this. What does HTTPS protect?
questions.answer: HTTPS encrypts data in transit. It does not prove the website or its owner is honest.
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts data in transit. It does not prove the website or its owner is honest.

questions.question: Give a physical security measure and the threat it limits.
questions.answer: Lock the server room to limit access and reduce theft or tampering.
questions.explanation: Lock the server room to limit access and reduce theft or tampering.

questions.question: What is penetration testing?
questions.answer: C — Security testing with permission
questions.explanation: Authorised testers work within agreed limits to find security weaknesses.

questions.question: “POP's main job is sending a new message from a client to a mail server.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: POP downloads email from a server to a device. IMAP keeps email views in sync across devices.
questions.explanation: POP downloads email from a server to a device. IMAP keeps email views in sync across devices.

questions.question: A pupil wants matching inboxes and read status on a phone and laptop. “IMAP only sends new outgoing mail.” Correct this. Why use IMAP here?
questions.answer: IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs messages and read status across devices. SMTP sends outgoing mail.
questions.explanation: IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs messages and read status across devices. SMTP sends outgoing mail.

questions.question: What does operating-system file management do?
questions.answer: It manages files and folders: naming, saving, copying, moving and deleting them.
questions.explanation: It manages files and folders: naming, saving, copying, moving and deleting them.

questions.question: Why split network protocols into layers?
questions.answer: D — Each layer has a job
questions.explanation: Separate tasks and clear interfaces make development and fault-finding easier.

questions.question: “Encryption alone guarantees files cannot be stolen or deleted.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Without the key, an attacker cannot easily read ciphertext. Encryption does not stop theft or deletion.
questions.explanation: Without the key, an attacker cannot easily read ciphertext. Encryption does not stop theft or deletion.

questions.question: A fake useful app locks files for a ransom. “Malware is any app that uses lots of RAM.” Correct this. How does this malware cause harm?
questions.answer: Malware is made to harm, disrupt or gain access without permission. Different types work in different ways and can affect data access, privacy or availability.
questions.explanation: Malware is made to harm, disrupt or gain access without permission. Different types work in different ways and can affect data access, privacy or availability.

questions.question: What does a compression utility do?
questions.answer: It reduces the storage space required for data, using a suitable lossless or lossy method.
questions.explanation: It reduces the storage space required for data, using a suitable lossless or lossy method.

questions.question: What does a denial-of-service attack try to do?
questions.answer: A — Make a service unavailable
questions.explanation: Flooding a service can stop genuine users from accessing it.

questions.question: “Data interception is only copying a paper document from a filing cabinet.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Capturing data during transmission, potentially exposing confidential information.
questions.explanation: Capturing data during transmission, potentially exposing confidential information.

questions.question: A new user needs to open and sort files. “A user interface replaces all CPU instructions.” Correct this. How does an interface help?
questions.answer: A user interface lets people use the computer, through GUI controls or typed commands. Other OS tasks manage devices, accounts, memory and files.
questions.explanation: A user interface lets people use the computer, through GUI controls or typed commands. Other OS tasks manage devices, accounts, memory and files.

questions.question: Give a cultural impact of digital technology.
questions.answer: Digital communication can change language, access, traditions and how people take part in communities.
questions.explanation: Digital communication can change language, access, traditions and how people take part in communities.

questions.question: What does anti-malware detect?
questions.answer: B — Malicious software
questions.explanation: Anti-malware detects and may quarantine or remove malware. It needs updates.

questions.question: “Every pupil needs full administrator rights for a secure network.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Give users only the access rights they need. This limits access without permission and possible damage.
questions.explanation: Give users only the access rights they need. This limits access without permission and possible damage.

questions.question: A new printer will not work. “A printer driver only stores website passwords.” Correct this. How could the right driver help?
questions.answer: A driver lets the OS communicate with and control a peripheral, such as a printer.
questions.explanation: A driver lets the OS communicate with and control a peripheral, such as a printer.

questions.question: What is a typical feature of proprietary software?
questions.answer: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.
questions.explanation: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.

questions.question: Why use a different password for each account?
questions.answer: C — Limit damage after a leak
questions.explanation: A leaked password then cannot be reused to access your other accounts.

questions.question: “Defragmentation must speed up every SSD by moving its read head.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It brings file fragments together, reducing read-head movement when accessing a file.
questions.explanation: It brings file fragments together, reducing read-head movement when accessing a file.

questions.question: A program saves results and later reads attendance data. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Closing a file deletes it. (b) A program can read a file without opening it.
questions.answer: (a) Closing releases the file handle and helps finish buffered writes; it does not delete the file. (b) Opening creates a handle for access. Open, read or write, then close. Screen output does not save a file.
questions.explanation: (a) Closing releases the file handle and helps finish buffered writes; it does not delete the file. (b) Opening creates a handle for access. Open, read or write, then close. Screen output does not save a file.

questions.question: Which law addresses unauthorised access to a computer system?
questions.answer: The Computer Misuse Act 1990.
questions.explanation: The Computer Misuse Act 1990.

questions.question: What can frequent device replacement increase?
questions.answer: D — Electronic waste
questions.explanation: Making replacements uses resources and energy; disposing of old devices adds waste.

questions.question: “Unauthorised access is lawful whenever the attacker does not delete files.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Unauthorised access to computer systems and related prohibited activities.
questions.explanation: Unauthorised access to computer systems and related prohibited activities.

questions.question: A pupil uses a browser and editor at once. Staff and pupils need different access rights. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Each app needs its own CPU. (b) Every user needs full access.
questions.answer: (a) The OS shares memory, resources and CPU time between apps. (b) User management controls accounts, login checks and access rights.

teachingAdditions: Storage units and decimal conversions

A bit is one binary digit; a nibble is 4 bits and a byte is 8 bits. Using decimal units: 1 KB = 1,000 bytes; 1 MB = 1,000 KB; 1 GB = 1,000 MB; 1 TB = 1,000 GB; 1 PB = 1,000 TB. For example, 2 MB = 2,000 KB = 2,000,000 bytes; 2 TB = 2,000 GB.
Character capacity and adjacent codes

With n bits there are 2^n distinct binary patterns: 7 bits permit 128 codes. A character set must provide enough distinct codes for its characters. questions.answer: (a) Sample rate means samples per second: 8,000 Hz means 8,000 samples each second. A higher rate can add detail and use more space. (b) Bit depth is bits per sample; more bits allow more amplitude levels and use more space. Longer duration adds samples.
questions.explanation: (a) Sample rate means samples per second: 8,000 Hz means 8,000 samples each second. A higher rate can add detail and use more space. (b) Bit depth is bits per sample; more bits allow more amplitude levels and use more space. Longer duration adds samples.

questions.question: What is a key feature of an open-source licence?
questions.answer: It permits access to source code and modification or redistribution under its conditions.
questions.explanation: It permits access to source code and modification or redistribution under its conditions.

questions.question: How does the OS support multitasking?
questions.answer: D — Shares CPU time
questions.explanation: The OS shares processor time and manages memory for running applications.

questions.question: “A longer recording automatically has finer amplitude accuracy.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It doubles size but does not by itself improve sampling quality.
questions.explanation: It doubles size but does not by itself improve sampling quality.
topics: Duration effect on size versus quality

questions.question: A mono clip uses 1,000 samples/s for 3 s at 8 bits/sample. Calculate its raw size in bytes, excluding headers and compression.
questions.answer: (a) 1,000 × 3 × 8 = 24,000 bits; divide by 8 = 3,000 bytes.
questions.explanation: (a) 1,000 × 3 × 8 = 24,000 bits; divide by 8 = 3,000 bytes.

questions.question: What makes a technology issue ethical?
questions.answer: It concerns fairness, responsibility or what ought to be done, even if an action is legal.
questions.explanation: It concerns fairness, responsibility or what ought to be done, even if an action is legal.

questions.question: Which technology does a USB flash drive use?
questions.answer: A — Solid-state
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive uses non-volatile solid-state memory, with no moving parts.

questions.question: “Compression must increase every file's size.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Reducing file size can reduce storage requirements and transmission time.
questions.explanation: Reducing file size can reduce storage requirements and transmission time.

questions.question: A website thumbnail may tolerate a small reduction in detail. “Lossy compression guarantees an identical original after decompression.” Correct this. What could happen?
questions.answer: Lossy compression removes information, so the exact original may be lost. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code must be restored exactly.
questions.explanation: Lossy compression removes information, so the exact original may be lost. A thumbnail can lose some detail; source code must be restored exactly.

questions.question: What is decomposition?
questions.answer: Breaking a complex problem into smaller manageable subproblems.
questions.explanation: Breaking a complex problem into smaller manageable subproblems.

questions.question: Which is an OS file-management task?
questions.answer: B — Renaming a folder
questions.explanation: File management includes naming, moving, saving and deleting files and folders.

questions.question: “Lossless compression deliberately removes arbitrary source-code characters.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Lossless compression restores the original exactly. Losing source-code characters could break the program.
questions.explanation: Lossless compression restores the original exactly. Losing source-code characters could break the program.

questions.question: A computer needs maintenance and data protection. “Utilities are only apps for writing essays.” Correct this. What do utilities do?
questions.answer: Utilities maintain or protect a computer, adding tools beyond the OS. Writing an essay is an application task.
questions.explanation: Utilities maintain or protect a computer, adding tools beyond the OS. Writing an essay is an application task.

questions.question: What is algorithmic thinking?
questions.answer: Developing a clear, ordered and unambiguous method for solving a problem.
questions.explanation: Developing a clear, ordered and unambiguous method for solving a problem.

questions.question: What does an encryption utility produce?
questions.answer: C — Ciphertext
questions.explanation: Encryption uses an algorithm and key to turn readable data into ciphertext.

questions.question: What does a compression utility do?
questions.answer: It reduces the storage space required for data, using a suitable lossless or lossy method.
questions.explanation: It reduces the storage space required for data, using a suitable lossless or lossy method.

questions.question: A CPU reads an instruction at memory address 120. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) MAR holds a calculation result. (b) MDR always holds the next instruction's address.
questions.answer: (a) The MAR holds the address being accessed. (b) The MDR holds data or an instruction moving to or from memory. An address is different from the data at it.
questions.explanation: (a) The MAR holds the address being accessed. (b) The MDR holds data or an instruction moving to or from memory. An address is different from the data at it.

questions.question: For cost = price × quantity, identify input, processing and output.
questions.answer: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiplication. Output: total cost.
questions.explanation: Inputs: price and quantity. Processing: multiplication. Output: total cost.

questions.question: What decides whether an action is legal?
questions.answer: D — The law
questions.explanation: Legal issues concern what the law allows or prohibits.

questions.question: What is a privacy concern with collecting personal data?
questions.answer: People may lose control over how identifying information is used or shared.
questions.explanation: People may lose control over how identifying information is used or shared.

questions.question: An online service uses only one language. “Technology cannot affect language or who takes part.” Correct this. Who might be left out?
questions.answer: Technology can change language, access, traditions and who can take part. Consider who benefits or is harmed. Something legal may still be unfair.
questions.explanation: Technology can change language, access, traditions and who can take part. Consider who benefits or is harmed. Something legal may still be unfair.

questions.question: What does a diamond represent in a flowchart?
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: Why is primary storage needed?
questions.answer: A — To hold data in use
questions.explanation: Primary storage holds instructions and data needed while programs run.

questions.question: “Both RAM and ROM lose their contents when power is removed.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: RAM loses its contents; ROM keeps its contents because it is non-volatile.
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents; ROM keeps its contents because it is non-volatile.

questions.question: A computer needs startup instructions when switched on. “ROM normally holds all unsaved user work while applications run.” Correct this. What could happen?
questions.answer: ROM keeps firmware or startup instructions without power. These let the computer start when switched on.
questions.explanation: ROM keeps firmware or startup instructions without power. These let the computer start when switched on.

questions.question: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.answer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.explanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.question: Where is CPU cache?
questions.answer: B — In or near the CPU
questions.explanation: Cache sits in or near the CPU for fast access to often-used data and instructions.

questions.question: “Secondary storage is needed because RAM permanently keeps every file.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It keeps programs and files when power is off and usually provides lots of storage space.
questions.explanation: It keeps programs and files when power is off and usually provides lots of storage space.

questions.question: A school uses DVDs for read-only videos and an HDD for a large archive. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) DVDs are magnetic. (b) HDDs use only flash chips and have no moving parts.
questions.answer: (a) A DVD uses optical storage, read by a laser. (b) An HDD uses magnetic storage on spinning platters. Moving parts and portability affect which is suitable.
questions.explanation: (a) A DVD uses optical storage, read by a laser. (b) An HDD uses magnetic storage on spinning platters. Moving parts and portability affect which is suitable.

questions.question: Name one operating-system function.
questions.answer: Memory management, user management, file management, a user interface or peripheral management.
questions.explanation: Memory management, user management, file management, a user interface or peripheral management.

questions.question: What does software copyright restrict?
questions.answer: C — Copying without permission
questions.explanation: Copyright protects original software and restricts copying or sharing without permission, subject to the licence and legal exceptions.

questions.question: What is a typical feature of proprietary software?
questions.answer: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.
questions.explanation: Source code is normally controlled by its owner and users receive specified usage rights.

questions.question: A school needs a large, cheap archive drive. A pupil's only coursework copy is on an SSD. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) An HDD is always faster and tougher than an SSD. (b) An SSD never fails, so needs no backup.
questions.answer: (a) An HDD can give lots of space at low cost per GB. Check the device and task. (b) An SSD can fail through faults or wear, so keep backups. No device is best at everything.
questions.explanation: (a) An HDD can give lots of space at low cost per GB. Check the device and task. (b) An SSD can fail through faults or wear, so keep backups. No device is best at everything.

questions.question: What is the difference between input and output?
questions.answer: Input enters a program; output is information the program produces.
questions.explanation: Input enters a program; output is information the program produces.

questions.question: Why is SSD random access often faster than HDD access?
questions.answer: D — No read head must move
questions.explanation: An SSD has no moving head seeking data on spinning platters.

questions.question: “Portability and durability mean exactly the same thing.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: No moving read/write parts makes an SSD less likely to be damaged by shocks. Size and weight also affect portability.
questions.explanation: No moving read/write parts makes an SSD less likely to be damaged by shocks. Size and weight also affect portability.

questions.question: A journey planner needs stops and times, but not bus-seat colours. “Abstraction removes every detail, even inputs.” Correct this. What should the planner keep?
questions.answer: Remove details that are not needed. Keep the information and parts needed to solve the problem, then link clear steps.
questions.explanation: Remove details that are not needed. Keep the information and parts needed to solve the problem, then link clear steps.

teachingAdditions: Constants and suitable types

A constant is a named value intended to remain unchanged during execution, such as MAX_CLASS_SIZE=30. A variable such as score changes. Integer stores whole numbers; real can store fractional values such as 2.75. A character is one character such as a middle initial; a string is a sequence such as a full name.

questions.question: What does assignment do to a variable?
questions.answer: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.
questions.explanation: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.

questions.question: What is the CPU's main job?
questions.answer: A — Execute instructions
questions.explanation: The CPU executes instructions to process data.

questions.question: A folder contains 30 images of 200 KB each. Using decimal units, give its total size in KB and MB.
prerequisite_notes: Add a worked multiple-file capacity example before retrieval.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: A photographer travels with large files and needs fast transfers. “The cheapest storage is always best.” Correct this. What else matters?
questions.answer: Check capacity, speed, cost and how it will be used. An SSD can suit fast transfers and travel, if its capacity and price meet the photographer's needs.
questions.explanation: Check capacity, speed, cost and how it will be used. An SSD can suit fast transfers and travel, if its capacity and price meet the photographer's needs.

teachingAdditions: Integer arithmetic and exponentiation

In OCR ERL, 17 DIV 5 is the integer quotient 3, while 17 MOD 5 is the remainder 2. The ^ operator means exponentiation: 2 ^ 3 = 8. Ordinary precedence applies; 4 + 3 * 2 = 10, whereas (4 + 3) * 2 = 14.

questions.question: What are 17 DIV 5 and 17 MOD 5?
questions.answer: DIV gives integer quotient 3; MOD gives remainder 2.
questions.explanation: DIV gives integer quotient 3; MOD gives remainder 2.
prerequisite_notes: Explicitly teach integer quotient and remainder with examples; do not infer coverage from ordinary division.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: What happens in the fetch stage?
questions.answer: B — Get the next instruction
questions.explanation: The CPU gets the next instruction from memory.

questions.question: “Execution only copies an instruction into memory without performing it.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.
questions.explanation: The operation specified by the decoded instruction is carried out.

questions.question: A CPU compares scores and adds a bonus. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) The Control Unit stores documents forever. (b) The ALU stores the next instruction's address.
questions.answer: (a) The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. (b) The ALU handles arithmetic and logic. Registers store data or addresses briefly.
questions.explanation: (a) The Control Unit decodes instructions and controls CPU operations. (b) The ALU handles arithmetic and logic. Registers store data or addresses briefly.

teachingAdditions: Boolean is a data type

A Boolean stores true or false. For example, complete=false is a Boolean state; it is different from the string "false". Comparisons such as score>=50 produce Boolean results that can be combined using AND, OR and NOT.

questions.question: When is A AND B true?
questions.answer: Only when both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Only when both A and B are true.

questions.question: What does CPU cache hold?
questions.answer: C — Often-used data and instructions
questions.explanation: Cache holds frequently or recently used data and instructions for fast access.

questions.question: “A register is a large external drive used for backups.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
questions.explanation: A small, fast storage location inside the CPU. It holds data or addresses in use.
topics: Registers as small fast CPU storage

questions.question: The next instruction is at address 240. An addition gives 18. What do the accumulator and Program Counter hold? Explain the difference.
questions.answer: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.
questions.explanation: The accumulator holds the result, 18. The PC holds the next instruction's address, 240.

questions.question: What does selection do?
questions.answer: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.

questions.question: What does a structure diagram show?
questions.answer: D — Parts and their hierarchy
questions.explanation: It shows how a problem is split into sections and smaller parts.
prerequisite_notes: Teach a structure diagram and its subsection links; flowcharts are a different representation.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: “Doubling clock speed guarantees every program finishes in exactly half the time.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: More clock cycles per second. This may let the CPU process more instructions if other factors are similar.
questions.explanation: More clock cycles per second. This may let the CPU process more instructions if other factors are similar.

questions.question: A user runs several apps. Some work can be shared across cores. “Each extra core doubles every program's speed.” Correct this. When do more cores help?
questions.answer: More cores help when work can be split between them. Other CPU features and the task also affect the speed gained.
questions.explanation: More cores help when work can be split between them. Other CPU features and the task also affect the speed gained.

questions.question: What does selection do?
questions.answer: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.

questions.question: What does the Program Counter hold?
questions.answer: A — The next instruction's address
questions.explanation: The PC holds the address of the next instruction to fetch.

questions.question: “Larger cache increases the number of installed CPU cores.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.
questions.explanation: A larger cache holds more often-used data and instructions. This can reduce slower memory access.

questions.question: CPU A: 4 GHz, two cores, 2 MB cache. CPU B: 3 GHz, eight cores, 8 MB cache. Why is neither fastest for every task?
questions.answer: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.
questions.explanation: A has more cycles per second, which may help one task. B has more cores for parallel work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Speed also depends on the task and CPU design.

questions.question: When is a count-controlled loop suitable?
questions.answer: When the number of repetitions is known or determined by a fixed count.
questions.explanation: When the number of repetitions is known or determined by a fixed count.

questions.question: Why use pseudocode?
questions.answer: B — Plan steps without exact syntax
questions.explanation: Pseudocode describes algorithm steps without needing one language's exact syntax.

questions.question: “A diamond is used only for unconditional calculations.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: A program works out a bill, then applies a discount. “The order of steps never matters.” Correct this. What could go wrong?
questions.answer: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.
questions.explanation: Steps must be clear and in the right order. Check that conditions give the right result for every allowed input.

questions.question: When is a condition-controlled loop suitable?
questions.answer: When repetition continues or ends according to a condition, such as valid input.
questions.explanation: When repetition continues or ends according to a condition, such as valid input.

questions.question: Linear-search [7, 2, 9, 4] for 4. How many comparisons are needed?
questions.explanation: Starting at the first item, compare 7, 2, 9 and then 4.

questions.question: “An IF statement must execute every possible branch regardless of its condition.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch using a condition. Selection can be nested.

questions.question: Do one bubble-sort pass from left to right, smallest to largest, on [6, 1, 5, 3]. Show the array after each comparison. Which value ends up on the right?
questions.answer: (a) [[1, 6, 5, 3], [1, 5, 6, 3], [1, 5, 3, 6]]; largest value 6 is at the right end.
questions.explanation: (a) [[1, 6, 5, 3], [1, 5, 6, 3], [1, 5, 3, 6]]; largest value 6 is at the right end.

questions.question: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.answer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.explanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.question: Which type suits a count of pupils?
questions.answer: D — Integer
questions.explanation: An integer stores a whole-number count.
prerequisite_notes: Explicitly contrast real values with integers in a supplied scenario.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: How do character and string data differ?
questions.answer: A character represents one character; a string represents a sequence of characters.
questions.explanation: A character represents one character; a string represents a sequence of characters.
prerequisite_notes: Explicitly distinguish a single character from a string.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: A limit of 30 appears five times in code. One copy changes to 32; the rest are missed. How would a named constant help? How does it differ from a changing score?
questions.answer: Define one named constant, such as MAX_CLASS_SIZE, and use it throughout. Change its definition once to update the limit. Use a variable for a score because it changes while the program runs.
questions.explanation: Define one named constant, such as MAX_CLASS_SIZE, and use it throughout. Change its definition once to update the limit. Use a variable for a score because it changes while the program runs.

questions.question: What does sequence mean in programming?
questions.answer: Instructions execute in the specified order.
questions.explanation: Instructions execute in the specified order.

questions.question: What is 4 + 3 * 2?
questions.explanation: Multiplication comes first: 3 × 2 = 6, then 4 + 6 = 10.

questions.question: What is 2 ^ 3 in OCR ERL?
questions.answer: 8; ^ denotes exponentiation in OCR ERL.
questions.explanation: 8; ^ denotes exponentiation in OCR ERL.
prerequisite_notes: Explicitly teach the exponentiation operator in OCR ERL.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: Join text '12' to '3'. Then convert '12' to an integer and add 3. Give both results. What should happen if the input is 'twelve'?
questions.answer: Joining the strings gives '123'. Converting '12' to an integer and adding 3 gives 15. Handle or reject 'twelve': it cannot be cast to an integer directly.
questions.explanation: Joining the strings gives '123'. Converting '12' to an integer and adding 3 gives 15. Handle or reject 'twelve': it cannot be cast to an integer directly.

questions.question: A £5-per-ticket program uses total = tickets + 5. What is the correction?
questions.answer: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.
questions.explanation: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.

questions.question: Insert 6 into sorted [2, 5, 8]. What is the result?
questions.explanation: Move 8 right and place 6 between 5 and 8.

questions.question: “A comparison operator must always produce a text paragraph.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: A Boolean result: true or false.
questions.explanation: A Boolean result: true or false.

questions.question: A warning needs high temperature OR high pressure. “OR is false when both inputs are true.” Correct this. What happens when both are high?
questions.answer: OR is true if at least one input is true, including both. AND needs both true. NOT reverses a value.
questions.explanation: OR is true if at least one input is true, including both. AND needs both true. NOT reverses a value.

questions.question: What does assignment do to a variable?
questions.answer: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.
questions.explanation: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.

questions.question: What is NOT true?
questions.answer: C — false
questions.explanation: NOT reverses a Boolean value: true becomes false.

questions.question: What values does a Boolean variable represent?
questions.answer: True or false.
questions.explanation: True or false.
prerequisite_notes: Name Boolean as a data type as well as using Boolean conditions.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: Computers share files on one school site. Two sites in different towns also need a link. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) A LAN spans several countries. (b) A WAN only works in one room.
questions.answer: (a) A LAN covers a small area, such as a school site. (b) A WAN links networks over a large area, often using outside providers' links. Internet access alone does not decide the type.
questions.explanation: (a) A LAN covers a small area, such as a school site. (b) A WAN links networks over a large area, often using outside providers' links. Internet access alone does not decide the type.

questions.question: What is the result of concatenating 'AB' and '12'?
questions.answer: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.
questions.explanation: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.

questions.question: How is an item accessed in a 1D array?
questions.answer: D — Using an index
questions.explanation: Each array element has an index. OCR ERL indexes start at 0.

questions.question: “Testing a few inputs proves a program can never contain any fault.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.
questions.explanation: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.

questions.question: A programmer tests input code while building a booking program, then tests the finished program. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Iterative testing starts only after delivery. (b) Final testing removes the need for earlier tests.
questions.answer: (a) Iterative testing checks and fixes parts while building the program. (b) Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Both are needed.
questions.explanation: (a) Iterative testing checks and fixes parts while building the program. (b) Final testing checks the finished program against its requirements. Both are needed.

questions.question: What does input validation check?
questions.answer: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.
questions.explanation: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.
topics: Validation rules and rejection of invalid data

questions.question: Valid ages are integers from 13 to 18. Which input has the right type but is invalid?
questions.explanation: 12 is an integer, but it is outside the valid range.

questions.question: “Defensive design assumes every user always enters valid and harmless data.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.
questions.explanation: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.

questions.question: A desktop needs a LAN connection. “A NIC keeps files when power is off.” Correct this. What does a NIC do here?
questions.answer: A NIC lets a device connect to a network. It has a different job from storage or a router.
questions.explanation: A NIC lets a device connect to a network. It has a different job from storage or a router.

questions.question: What is a one-dimensional array?
questions.answer: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.explanation: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.

questions.question: Valid ages are 13–18. Which is normal test data?
questions.explanation: 15 is an ordinary valid age, away from the boundaries.

questions.question: “Any device connected to the Internet is automatically an embedded system.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.
questions.explanation: It is part of a heating system, with the specific task of controlling temperature.

questions.question: A pupil enters a domain name. “DNS gives the same MAC address to every visitor.” Correct this. How does DNS help find the website?
questions.answer: DNS servers look up the IP address for a domain name. Access needs the relevant server and network services to work.
questions.explanation: DNS servers look up the IP address for a domain name. Access needs the relevant server and network services to work.

questions.question: How can a loop total an array's values?
questions.answer: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.
questions.explanation: Set a total to 0. Loop through the array, adding each value once.

questions.question: What is an embedded system designed for?
questions.answer: C — A specific task
questions.explanation: An embedded system performs a specific task within a larger device.

questions.question: “Adding active users always increases the bandwidth available to each user.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.
questions.explanation: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.

questions.question: A school needs central accounts and shared files. Three club laptops share files directly. Correct both claims. Explain why. (a) Every client must be a dedicated server. (b) Peer-to-peer needs a central server.
questions.answer: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.
questions.explanation: (a) A server manages shared services and resources for clients. (b) Peers share directly and can act as clients and servers. Central control suits a school; peer-to-peer can cost less for a small club but is harder to manage as it grows.

questions.question: How is a cell selected in a two-dimensional array?
questions.answer: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.
questions.explanation: Use two indexes: one for the row and one for the column.

questions.question: What is a router's main job?
questions.answer: D — Link different networks
questions.explanation: Routers forward data between networks using IP addresses.

questions.question: “An IPv4 address is always six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.” Correct this. Explain why.
questions.answer: IPv4 supports addressing and routing. It is usually written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.

teachingAdditions: Local and global constants as well as variables

teachingAdditions: Passing and returning an array

A function may receive an array as an argument, process it and return an array result. For example, receive [2,4,6], create a new array by adding 1 to each element, then return [3,5,7]. The caller must use the returned result. Passing the input and returning the output are separate actions; the original changes only if the implementation changes it.
